purpose: silver_ourairports_airports is the cleaned, one-row-per-ident reference table of 9057 world airports, heliports and seaplane bases landed from the OurAirports feed. It carries identity (ident, id, iata_code, icao_code, gps_code, local_code), classification (type, is_airport_type, is_scheduled_service), geography (latitude_deg, longitude_deg, elevation_ft, continent, iso_country, iso_region, municipality) and reference links, and it feeds gold airport dimensions and any join that resolves a flight or route code to a place.
usage: Join on ident, the declared grain and the only key that is both complete (null_rate 0.0) and unique (distinct_count 9057 of 9057 rows); id and iata_code are equally unique in this snapshot but are secondary. Read is_scheduled_service as a boolean derived from the source 'yes'/'no' values and is_airport_type as true only for large_airport, medium_airport and small_airport, so filter deliberately when heliports and seaplane bases should be excluded. Treat icao_code, gps_code, local_code, municipality, elevation_ft, keywords, home_link and wikipedia_link as optional and handle nulls explicitly; coordinates are DECIMAL(12,6) degrees and elevation_ft is integer feet that can be negative (min -1266).
limitations: Only Airbyte capture columns were removed; no business rows were filtered and no values were imputed, so coverage gaps survive into silver: local_code is null for 5766 rows (63.7%), keywords for 6155 (68.0%), home_link for 6784 (74.9%), icao_code for 1237 (13.7%), wikipedia_link for 1185 (13.1%), gps_code for 488 (5.4%), municipality for 360 (4.0%) and elevation_ft for 335 (3.7%). The profile reports duplicate_row_rate 0.0, so no dedupe was applied and any future duplicate landing will surface as a grain violation rather than being silently collapsed. Uniqueness of ident, id and iata_code is asserted from this snapshot's distinct_count only and must be measured against the warehouse before approval; keywords is left as a single unsplit text field, and link columns are not validated as reachable URLs.
